issues.title: Black--Scholes example falsely claimed to satisfy the v1 assumptions

failure_location.quote: Then, it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde} hold.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the Black--Scholes example satisfies both old Assumptions assumptions and assumptionpde. In fact, both require uniform ellipticity on all of R^d, while the stated coefficient is sigma(s,x)=sigma diag(x^1,...,x^d). At x=0 its covariance is zero, so for every nonzero xi it cannot dominate kappa|xi|^2 with kappa>0. Thus v1 does not establish that this example lies within its assumption-dependent theory; Z-independence was not an alternative under the old assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional formal results remain intact, but their advertised applicability to the paper's Black--Scholes example and associated numerical setup is unsupported in v1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recast this example in the standard log-price state. For strictly positive initial asset prices, set U_t^i=log X_t^i, so dU_t^i=(r-σ²/2)dt+σ dW_t^i and the covariance is the uniformly elliptic matrix σ²I. Replace the terminal payoff and obstacles by their compositions with the exponential map and state that the theory is applied in these coordinates; the transformed payoffs retain the required Lipschitz and piecewise-C^{1,2} properties. This preserves the same Black–Scholes game and numerical target.
issues.why_classification: The asset-coordinate assertion is genuinely false, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the standard log-price reparametrization is a short, routine, local repair that restores both ellipticity assumptions without changing the financial model, method, conclusions, rates, or any listed dependent formal result.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Either $f(t,x,y,z)=f(t,x,y,0)$ for all $(t,x,y,z)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d$, or $\sigma$ is uniformly elliptic on $[0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d$ .

issues.title: Missing minus sign in the lower penalization comparison bound
issues.failure_explanation: The proof defines C_w=D_w^+/(lambda-K_y)>=0. From lambda>2K_y one obtains C_w<=2D_w^+/lambda and hence -C_w>=-e^{K_yT}2D_w^+/lambda. The old printed statement C_w>=-e^{K_yT}2D_w^+/lambda is merely a vacuous positive-versus-negative inequality and cannot convert the analogous lower comparison shift into the theorem's stated lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: As printed, the lower half of ydiffbound and therefore its two-sided absolute estimate are not justified. This propagates to penaltyerror and the two total-error corollaries that use the O(lambda^{-1}) value-process estimate; the upper bound is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant comparison by -C_w ≥ -e^{K_y T}·2D_w^+/λ, equivalently first derive C_w≤2D_w^+/λ from λ>2K_y and then negate it. Use this estimate in the stated symmetric lower comparison argument. The two-sided bound in ydiffbound and the dependent penalty and total-error results then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The printed positive-versus-negative inequality is true but cannot justify the lower bound, so an actual proof inference must be repaired rather than merely ignored as harmless notation. The required algebra and symmetric comparison are short and routine, preserve the exact O(λ^{-1}) guarantee, and require no new lemma or proof architecture.

issues.title: Missing minus sign in the Z-independent tuning exponent

failure_location.quote: It follows that optimal error rate of $O(\Delta t^\frac{1}{2})$ can be obtained with choices $\lambda=\Delta t^{\frac{1}{2}}$ and $\Delta\tilde{t}=\Delta t/m$ for $m\ge\lambda^2,m\in\mathbb{N}$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under this coupling, choosing $\lambda \asymp \Delta t^{-1/2}$ yields

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that lambda=Delta t^{1/2}, together with the stated fine-grid choice, achieves O(Delta t^{1/2}). The old paper actually establishes in cor:final a bound containing lambda Delta t, lambda Delta-tilde-t^{1/2}, and 1/lambda, under lambda>2K_y. With the claimed positive exponent, 1/lambda=Delta t^{-1/2} diverges and lambda tends to zero, whereas lambda=Delta t^{-1/2} balances lambda Delta t and 1/lambda at order Delta t^{1/2}. Thus the advertised tuning does not follow from—and is outside the admissible asymptotic regime of—the stated result.
issues.overall_effect: The subsection opener gives an unusable tuning recommendation, but cor:final and the later labeled tuning remark already state the correct bound and coupling; no formal result is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace λ=Δt^{1/2} by λ=Δt^{-1/2}, retaining the stated fine-grid coupling Δt̃=Δt/m with m at least of order λ². Then λΔt, λΔt̃^{1/2}, and 1/λ are all O(Δt^{1/2}).
issues.why_classification: The negative exponent is uniquely forced by the displayed bound and is explicitly given later in the same old source. Correcting the missing minus sign changes no proof, formal result, rate, or substantive guarantee; it only repairs a transcriptionally inconsistent tuning recommendation.
